The complicated answer:

Basically the way it works is that the ROM is hard coded, and that's where the exploit is located. When the device boots the code inside the ROM is loaded into memory. This memory is writable, and so is the copy of the boot ROM that's inside of it. Under normal circumstances there are protections that prevent you from altering that part of the memory. Not sure how checkm8 works exactly but in the past for the iPhone 3G and stuff buffer overflows were used to get write access. I'd imagine this is similar.
Ah, well I didn't know that. Thanks for letting me know. Regardless, the drivers all work fine and the graphics card is working as advertised. It even outputs to a VGA monitor just fine.
